cf.title: docs: Include database collation check on SQL from alter_collation.sgml

input.subject: docs: Include database collation check on SQL from alter_collation.sgml

verdict_reasoning: The goal is sound and message #3 reproduced the gap: the current query returns no rows for an index on the database default collation. The remaining concerns are fixable design points at level 2. v2 drops named ICU collations that the current query reports (standards-compat-1) and lists indexes only while the lead-in still promises all dependent objects (standards-compat-2, prior-attempts-1). No level fails outright.

brief.title: Docs: make the alter collation query find objects using the database collation
brief.problem: The alter collation reference page gives a query that lists collations needing a refresh and their dependent objects. Objects that use the database default collation have no pg_depend entry, so the query misses them when the database collation version changes. This affects administrators checking for indexes to rebuild after an OS or library upgrade.
brief.proposed_design: v2 replaces the pg_depend-based query with one that expands pg_index.indcollation and joins pg_collation and pg_database. For the default collation it compares datcollversion with pg_database_collation_actual_version(), and for libc collations it compares collversion with pg_collation_actual_version(). The output lists indexes only, with stored and actual versions and the index definition.
user_visible_surface: Changed example query in doc/src/sgml/ref/alter_collation.sgml; the output columns change from Collation and Object to database, table, index, collname, collprovider, versions and index_definition.
author_claims: The current documented query does not report objects that use the database default collation.
v1 still missed indexes that use the database default collation; v2 handles them.
The v2 query is based on the query on the Locale_data_changes wiki page, changed to check version mismatch.
brief.thread_state: The reviewer confirmed that the old query returns no rows and v2 finds an affected index under a simulated libc mismatch. The reviewer flagged that named ICU collations (collprovider 'i') and an ICU database default are not matched by either branch, and the author has not replied.
unclear: Why v2 limits the check to the libc provider and drops ICU collations, which the old query covered.
Why v2 reports only indexes, while the old query also listed other dependent objects such as columns, constraints and views.
Whether the rendered docs build; the reviewer could not build them.
Whether the much longer query should live in the reference page or point to the wiki.

prior_attempts.title: Revert per-index collation version tracking feature.
prior_attempts.reason:
Design problems were discovered in the handling of composite types and
record types that would cause some relevant versions not to be recorded.
Misgivings were also expressed about the use of the pg_depend catalog
for this purpose.  We're out of time for this release so we'll revert
and try again.

Commits reverted:

1bf946bd: Doc: Document known problem with Windows collation versions.
cf002008: Remove no-longer-relevant test case.
ef387bed: Fix bogus collation-version-recording logic.
0fb0a050: Hide internal error for pg_collation_actual_version(<bad OID>).
ff942057: Suppress "warning: variable 'collcollate' set but not used".
d50e3b1f: Fix assertion in collation version lookup.
f24b1569: Rethink extraction of collation dependencies.
257836a7: Track collation versions for indexes.
cd6f479e: Add pg_depend.refobjversion.
7d1297df: Remove pg_collation.collversion.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 tracked collation versions per index in pg_depend and was a feature, reverted for design problems. This proposal only changes a documentation query; P1 supports only the technical point that collations inside composite types are easy to miss.

objections.title: v2 stops reporting ICU collation mismatches the current query catches
objections.failure_scenario: An administrator with ICU-based indexes upgrades libicu and runs the documented query. It returns no rows, so they run ALTER COLLATION ... REFRESH VERSION or ALTER DATABASE ... REFRESH COLLATION VERSION without rebuilding. The indexes stay corrupt until queries return wrong results.
objections.argument: The current query compares collversion with pg_collation_actual_version() for every provider, so named ICU collations are covered today. The v2 WHERE clause accepts only collprovider 'c', and the default branch only datlocprovider 'c', which drops named ICU collations and ICU database defaults. Message #3 reported this and the thread has no reply. A change to the reference query for the default-collation gap should not reduce coverage for other providers.
objections.author_must_show: Can the query cover the default collation without dropping named ICU collations and ICU database defaults, which the current query reports?

critic.reasoning: The old query compares collversion for every provider, and v2 accepts only 'c', so named ICU collations lose coverage. One correction: the old query did not report ICU database defaults either, so that part is a missed case and not a regression.

objections.title: Query narrows to indexes while the text still promises all dependents
objections.failure_scenario: A user has a check constraint, materialized view or partition bound that depends on a libc collation with a version change. The v2 query lists only indexes, so the user rebuilds those, refreshes the version, and the warning goes away. The other objects stay inconsistent and nothing reports them again.
objections.argument: The old query read pg_depend and listed every dependent object. v2 reads only pg_index.indcollation. The surrounding sentence is unchanged and still says the query finds "the objects that depend on them", and the server HINT says to rebuild "all objects affected". Message #2 explains the move to an index-only query only by the wiki source, not by a reason to drop the other objects.
objections.author_must_show: Why does the documented query drop non-index dependents, and if that is intended, how will the page tell readers which objects it no longer covers?

critic.reasoning: The hunk leaves the sentence "the objects that depend on them" unchanged while v2 reads only pg_index. The thread gives no reason for dropping the constraints and other dependents that the pg_depend query listed for named collations.

objections.title: Index-only query misses composite-type and non-index dependencies
objections.failure_scenario: After a glibc upgrade, an administrator runs the v2 query and sees no row for an index on a composite-typed column with a text field, or for a partitioned table keyed on text. The administrator refreshes the version without rebuilding. Wrong index scans or misrouted rows show up later.
objections.argument: v2 reads only pg_index.indcollation, which records one collation per index column. It does not record collations nested inside composite types, index predicates, constraints or partition keys. [P1] was reverted partly because composite and record types caused relevant versions not to be recorded, and the same gap applies to this query. The unchanged lead-in still promises "the objects that depend on them", but v2 returns indexes only.
objections.author_must_show: Which object kinds does the v2 query knowingly skip, and will the page say so or point to the wiki for those cases?

precedents.title: Revert per-index collation version tracking feature.

critic.reasoning: An index on a composite-typed column has no collation in pg_index.indcollation, so v2 skips it, and partition keys are not in pg_index. P1 reverted a feature and did not reject a docs query, so it supports only the technical point about composite types.

refuted.title: Hardcoded provider filter drops ICU coverage the current query has
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator on an ICU database, or one using named ICU collations, upgrades ICU and runs the documented query. It returns no rows, so they skip the reindex and keep indexes whose sort order no longer matches the library. They find out later through wrong query results or uniqueness violations.
refuted.argument: The current query compares collversion for every provider, so it catches named ICU collations. The v2 WHERE clause accepts only collprovider 'c', plus 'd' when datlocprovider is 'c', which drops ICU in both branches. Message #3 flagged this and the thread has no reply. Because the query lists providers by name, each new or changed provider needs a doc edit, and nothing fails when that edit is missed.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the query compare versions for every provider that records a version, with no list of provider codes, so that ICU and future providers are covered?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The added point about future providers needing doc edits has no concrete scenario beyond the ICU gap.

refuted.title: Query narrowed from all dependent objects to indexes only
refuted.failure_scenario: After a glibc upgrade, an administrator rebuilds every index the v2 query lists and runs ALTER COLLATION ... REFRESH VERSION. A materialized view, a check constraint or a range partition bound that uses the changed collation is not listed, so it stays out of date with no warning left to report it.
refuted.argument: The current text promises "the objects that depend on them", and the old pg_depend query reported columns, constraints and views. The v2 query reads only pg_index.indcollation, so it gains the default-collation case but loses every non-index dependent. The surrounding prose still describes dependent objects in general. The commit message does not mention this narrowing.
refuted.author_must_show: Why does the new query report only indexes, and could it keep the pg_depend branch for named collations while adding a default-collation branch?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. Its suggestion to keep a pg_depend branch for named collations is a useful direction for the author.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The example query reads pg_index, pg_collation and pg_database, but the patch changes no catalog.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The current query misses default-collation indexes in released branches too, so a committer must decide whether to backpatch the docs fix.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The v2 query names provider codes 'c' and 'd', so it needs an edit whenever provider coverage changes.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: The brief asks whether the longer query belongs in the reference page or on the Locale_data_changes wiki page.

questions: Can the query cover the database default collation without dropping the named ICU collations that the current query reports?
Should the default-collation branch also handle a database whose datlocprovider is ICU, which neither the old query nor v2 reports?
Why does v2 list indexes only, and could it keep the pg_depend branch for named collations and add a default-collation branch?
Which object kinds does v2 knowingly skip, such as indexes on composite-typed columns and partition keys, and will the page say so?
Should the lead-in sentence change, since it still says the query finds "the objects that depend on them"?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows collation version tracking and the locale providers (libc, ICU) would have to check the query. No committer has posted in the thread.
committability.liability: A reference-page query that administrators copy into upgrade checks. If it returns no rows for an affected object, the user may refresh the version without a rebuild, and the docs stay responsible for that until corrected.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 four days after v1 and moved the entry to the next CommitFest in September 2026. The author has not yet replied to the ICU point in message #3.

priority.reason: The fix helps any administrator who checks for indexes to rebuild after a C library upgrade, and the patch is one docs hunk. The ICU coverage and the index-only scope need an answer before a committer can take it.

provisional_note: The query was tested only with libc, in message #3. The ICU cases, non-index dependents and the rendered docs build were not checked by anyone in the thread.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track collation and ctype versions separately
precedents_retrieved.summary: Track the ctype version (in effect the Unicode version) separately from the collation version, in pg_collation and pg_database, so that changes to case mapping and pattern matching can be detected. The thread also asked whether the growing set of locale fields in pg_database should be cleaned up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took it up, and the author withdrew the patch for lack of discussion. Before that, the author noted that the extra field is confusing, because in pg_database it holds the ctype version of the default collation and not necessarily that of datctype.

precedents_retrieved.title: Preserve versions of initdb-created collations in pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_upgrade preserve the recorded versions of collations created by initdb. In binary-upgrade mode, pg_dump would delete all initdb-created collations in the new cluster and dump CREATE COLLATION commands with version information, instead of updating the existing objects in place.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review showed that the patch makes the pg_upgrade check fail for clusters initialized with SQL_ASCII encoding, where ICU collations for that encoding do not exist, and that it leaves the recreated collations looking like user-defined objects. The author then questioned the approach and suggested not creating collations in initdb at all. The reviewer replied that the problem would go away if the separate per-object collation version patch set were committed, since that drops the collversion column. The author then marked the patch Returned with Feedback without further changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this problem goes away if we commit the per-object collation
version patch set[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Collation code refactoring
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread began with a patch to track libc collation versions on macOS and moved on to letting Postgres load several ICU library versions, so each collation can stay on the ICU code it was created with. Late in the thread Jeff Davis posted a refactoring of the locale code that hides ICU calls behind pg_strcoll and a pg_icu_library method structure, with a hook for choosing the ICU library.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut closed the entry for procedural reasons. The multi-ICU patch, now planned as a user-defined collation provider in a new catalog table, was not posted in time, and the refactoring patch was already tracked in another commitfest entry. He also noted that the proposed CREATE COLLATION PROVIDER syntax exposes library paths, which affects dump/restore and needs a permissions design for non-superusers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So as a matter of procedure, we should probably close this commit fest entry for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: ICU as default collation provider
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch, written by Marina Polyakova and carried forward by Andrey Borodin, lets initdb and createdb take a collation provider and version inside the --locale string, so ICU can be the default collation for a cluster or database. It also makes ICU the default provider and changes the locale checks.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut judged the patch too large, with much unexplained code movement, and said it needed design and refactoring work first, such as adding a datcollprovider column to pg_database. The interface that encodes ICU in a libc-style lc_collate name was also questioned, and Andrey Borodin asked for community input on a better one. The patch also broke connections to existing databases. It was moved through several commitfests with only rebases, and Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the thread had stalled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think it's worth reviewing this patch any
further.  It needs several steps back and some fundamental design and
refactoring work.

precedents_retrieved.title: Multi-version ICU
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let one Postgres binary load several ICU library versions with dlopen, so collations and indexes built with an older ICU keep using it after an upgrade while new objects use a newer ICU. Designs discussed included search by collation version, providers named by ICU major version (provider = ICU63), and an icu_multilib extension driven by GUCs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread never agreed on a user-facing model, catalogues or DDL; search by collation version and per-version providers both stayed open. Peter Eisentraut noted that exposing OS-level library details causes dump/restore and permission problems. Jeff Davis asked for validation of the icu_multilib approach before doing more work, Robert Haas found its docs hard to follow, and Thomas Munro said he could not work on it this cycle.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we managed to prove that dlopen works for this, and learn some really interesting stuff about Unicode and ICU evolution, but we still have to come up with the right model, catalogues and DDL etc, for a nice user experience.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench - document compatibility with older server versions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread began as a patch to stop pgbench sending "\." at the end of COPY data, which only protocol version 2 needs. It became a documentation patch stating that pgbench requires a server of version 8.2 or later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers judged that the stated minimum server version would go out of date without anyone noticing, for example when a later change needs 8.4. Peter Eisentraut also said client programs are generally expected to work across server versions unless restrictions are documented, so the note added no useful information. He closed the entry because more people favoured not documenting it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems almost guaranteed to get out of
date without anybody noticing so.

precedents_retrieved.title: Warning for Datatype mismatch between subscriber table and publisher table for logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical replication emit a warning when a subscriber table column has a different data type from the matching publisher column. The goal is to show type mismatches early so users can debug replication problems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not revise the patch after review, and it had not passed CI since about mid March, so the CF entry was closed. Ashutosh Bapat had asked for the unrelated file renames to be removed. He also noted that the code maps columns by position, and that it compares type OIDs and names on the subscriber without using the remote type cache.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since this has not been fixed, and the patch has not passed CI since at least
mid March, I'll close this CF entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY support for partitioned indexes. It changes index_drop() to expand a partitioned index into the list of its partition indexes and run the concurrent drop steps on all of them in two transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier disliked the new code path for deleting dependent objects in the partition tree and said the problem needed more design work first. The patch then stopped applying to HEAD, and the author withdrew it until the related patch for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned tables makes progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking
quicky at the patch, I am not much a fan of the new code path
introduced for the deletion of dependent objects in the partition
tree, so my gut is telling me that we need to think harder about the
problem at hand first.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: On-disk bitmap indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
On-disk bitmap indexes
Section: Features We Do Not Want
Linked: Re: Bitmap index AM; Bitmap index thoughts; Stream bitmaps; Re: Bitmapscan changes - Requesting further feedback; Updated bitmap index patch; Reviewing new index types (was Re: [PATCHES] Updated bitmap indexpatch); Bitmap Indexes: request for feedback; bitmap indexes - performance; [PATCH] bitmap indexes
precedents_retrieved.objection: The rigidity of on-disk bitmap indexes, and the existence of GIN and in-memory bitmaps make this undesirable.

roaster_notes.note: One objection raised. No earlier attempt to change this documentation query was found in the precedent list.
There is no change to syntax, GUCs, pg_dump or the catalog. The two objections are about the documented query, which users copy into their upgrade checks.

The patch changes only an example query in doc/src/sgml/ref/alter_collation.sgml. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, protocol message or extension API, so nothing in this angle applies. Whether the query covers ICU collations and non-index objects belongs to other angles.

This is a docs-only change to an example query that reads catalogs any user can already read, using functions that already exist. It adds no new privilege, default or exposure, so the security angle finds nothing to object to.
A docs-only change to an example query adds no hot-path cost and no API, so the maintenance objections are limited to coverage and to future provider changes.

No existing feature lists the indexes that use the database default collation after a version change. The connect-time warning and ALTER DATABASE ... REFRESH COLLATION VERSION report the mismatch but list no objects, and the current documented query misses them, as message #3 confirmed. The Locale_data_changes wiki query is the source of v2, not a replacement for correct reference docs. Gaps for ICU collations and non-index objects belong to other angles.

The proposal fixes a documented query that misses indexes on the database default collation, and the reviewer reproduced the gap in message #3. This hits anyone who upgrades the OS C library, so demand is real. The narrower scope of v2 (no ICU branch, indexes only) is a design concern for other angles.
